Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.8.1–22 and 1.9.1: Chyavana's son by Sukanya is Pramati; Pramati's son by Ghritachi is Ruru; Ruru's son by Pramadvara is Shunaka (1.8.1–2); the apsara Menaka conceives by the gandharva king Vishvavasu (1.8.5) and leaves the new-born on a river bank by the hermitage of the sage Sthulakesha (1.8.6–7); he sees her abandoned there, shining, takes her up in pity and raises her (1.8.8–9); he names her Pramadvara because she is the best of women (1.8.10); Ruru sees her in the hermitage and is overcome by love (1.8.11); through his friends he lets his father know, Pramati asks Sthulakesha, and the wedding is fixed under the stars of Bhaga (1.8.12–13; in the picture only); a few days before it, playing with her friends, she does not see a sleeping snake lying across her way and steps on it (1.8.14–15); it bites her (1.8.16); she falls lifeless, and lifeless is lovelier than ever, as if asleep (1.8.17–18: `lay` now says "dead"); her father and the ascetics see her; the sages gather and weep, and Ruru goes out in his pain (1.8.19–22); he cries out in the deep forest (1.9.1) and a messenger of the gods speaks (1.9.6). Great-grandson of Bhrigu: Bhrigu, Chyavana, Pramati, Ruru (1.5.7). The names Menaka and Sthulakesha are on plaques, not spoken; Vishvavasu is first named on episode 45's plaque.
structure: From episode 41 (the step-up; script/ARC-41-50.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, spoken by ≤ 2.8 s; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Ruru: a young sage of Bhrigu's line

loop.prevQuestion: How did one of Bhrigu's line lose his bride to a snake?
loop.openQuestion: What did the messenger of the gods tell Ruru?

strings.recapLine: A sage's curse made fire eat everything. This is his great-grandson's story.

lines.text: A bride. A snake. A wedding.
lines.say: A bride. A snake. A wedding.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (three fragments, each landing on its own image inside one moving shot): an anklet stepping through violet grass; a banded snake asleep across the path; a garland half made. The card builds word by word, centre-left.

lines.text: Ruru was a young sage of Bhrigu's line.
lines.say: Ruru was a young sage [p:80] of Bhrigu's line.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): Ruru walking through a hermitage wood with his staff (plaque: Ruru · a young sage of Bhrigu's line). Pays off episode 43's last line by 5 s.

lines.text: By a river, an apsara, a nymph of heaven, left her newborn daughter.
lines.say: By a river, [p:80] an apsara, [p:60] a nymph of heaven, [p:100] left her newborn daughter.
lines.note: STORY 1 · NEW LIGHT, the river bank in pearl mist (riverbank-pearl): a luminous woman lays a bundle among the reeds and rises, not quite touching the ground (plaque: Menaka · an apsara); a tilt from her down to the child.

lines.text: A sage found her and raised her as his own.
lines.say: A sage found her [p:100] and raised her as his own.
lines.note: STORY 2: an old sage with a great mass of matted hair kneels in the reeds (kneel, then carry: an eased blend) and lifts the shining child (plaque: Sthulakesha · the sage who raised her).

lines.text: He named her Pramadvara: the finest of women.
lines.say: He named her Pramadvara: [p:200] the finest of women.
lines.note: STORY 3 · NEW LIGHT, a spring meadow (meadow-spring, petals): the girl grown, turning among flowers; an orbit round her (plaque: Pramadvara · "the finest of women").

lines.text: Ruru saw her, and loved her.
lines.say: Ruru saw her, [p:300] and loved her.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE CLOSE-UP: Ruru's face between two trunks: calm to wonder to a small smile (brow up, eyes wide, the mouth's corner); his gaze follows her across; the shot holds on him after the words. Behind, small and out of focus, two old sages with joined palms and a garland between them: the wedding day is set (seen, not said).

lines.text: A few days before it, she was out playing with her friends.
lines.say: A few days before it, [p:100] she was out playing with her friends.
lines.note: STORY 6: the meadow from above (a crane down): three girls running; a ball of flowers thrown; the grass moves. In the lower corner of the path, a small dark coil.

lines.text: She did not see the snake asleep in her path.
lines.say: She did not see the snake [p:100] asleep in her path.
lines.note: STORY 7 · THE TURN (≈ 52 %) after a real silence · THE SIGNATURE SHOT: frame-within-frame at ground level: through a dark arch of grass blades, her foot coming down in the middle distance, the small sleeping snake in the foreground a clear hand's breadth of ground away from it (the two shapes never touch or overlap in the frame), the light gone violet. cam: frame.

lines.text: It bit her, and she fell.
lines.say: It bit her, [p:250] and she fell.
lines.note: STORY 8 (answers the hook): one flash of the strike (two frames of green on black, no wound shown); the garland falls; a tilt down with it.

lines.text: She lay dead, as if asleep, lovelier than ever.
lines.say: She lay dead, [p:250] as if asleep, [p:150] lovelier than ever.
lines.note: STORY 9 (a second real silence before it; the text has it: lifeless, she was lovelier still): the colour drains (ash-grey): her face among fallen flowers, calm; petals settle; a slow push.

lines.text: The sages of the forest gathered and wept.
lines.say: The sages of the forest [p:80] gathered and wept.
lines.note: STORY 10 · NEW LIGHT, the forest at night (grief-blue, one lamp): a pull back from her face to the circle of seated sages, heads bowed; Ruru standing apart, at the edge of the light.

lines.text: Ruru walked into the deep forest and cried out. And a messenger of the gods answered.
lines.say: Ruru walked into the deep forest [p:80] and cried out. [p:350] And a messenger of the gods [p:100] answered.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger): Ruru among black trunks, his head thrown back; on "answered" a shaft of pale gold comes down through the canopy. The source line (top).
The NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image, with the source line; dissolve into frame 1.
